reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis is physically sound, combining well-established techniques (DSC/DTA, XRD, imaging) to measure standard thermodynamic properties, though the claimed uncertainties are ambitious and not rigorously justified from the described setup alone.
reasons.testability: The proposed round-robin test is clear and provides specific, quantitative falsification criteria, but the test design lacks crucial practical details (e.g., how volume change is measured from imaging, sample geometry) that make it incomplete.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis addresses the core question directly by proposing a practical, integrated experimental workflow, but it is essentially a description of standard techniques and lacks a novel physical rationale or predictive model, limiting its insight.
